method: Each link to a Congressional Record page (a CREC granule) anywhere in the corpus JSON is one occurrence. Its quoted words are the curly-quoted passages between the previous link run and this one, within the same paragraph or list item. A quotation is attributed when every piece of it (split at ellipses and bracketed insertions) appears both in GovInfo's text of the cited page and in exactly one maker's saved documents for that bill and day in docs/argument_key/evidence/*/manifest.tsv; an inserted document wins over the speech that contains it. The correct label is the one the site builder makes for that document (maker, kind, date). In a run of several links, quotations not on the Record page, or in no saved Record document, are left to the other links. A citation with no such quotation (a paraphrase in an evidence note) is matched to the released evidence note in docs/argument_key/quality_pass that holds nearly all its words (basis gives the share); the Record documents that note names for this page decide the label, each checked by its locating quotation. Two paraphrases were attributed by hand (basis 'by hand'). A citation run that links the same page more than once is judged link by link against its current label (same_page_run). Citations of a page with no saved manifest document keep their page-level label (basis 'page label'). occurrence is the 0-based position of the citation among the Record citations in that field.
